title.value: How Useful are Educational Questions Generated by Large Language Models?
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the document.
title.quote: How Useful are Educational Questions Generated by Large Language Models?

extractions.description: The paper explores the use of large language models for generating educational questions, specifically assessing their quality and usefulness as judged by teachers. It examines the potential of these models to reduce teacher workload and enhance educational content by using controllable text generation and question taxonomies such as Bloom's taxonomy and difficulty levels.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the educational application of AI for generating questions, which does not fit into any of the predefined eco-responsible categories related to climate change or sustainability. The study assesses educational value rather than environmental or ecological impact.
primary_category.quote: Controllable text generation (CTG) by large language models has a huge potential to transform education for teachers and students alike.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper doesn’t address secondary eco-responsible topics within the predefined categories as it mainly stays within the domain of education technology.
secondary_categories.quote: A robust question generation (QG) system has the potential to empower teachers by decreasing their cognitive load while creating teaching material.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any existing sub-categories within the eco-responsible framework as it deals with educational advancement through AI, rather than environmental or sustainability issues.
primary_sub_category.quote: Recent advancements in LLMs have raised questions about their impact on education, including promising use cases.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories are applicable as the paper is focused on educational technology and efficacy rather than eco-responsibility.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We conduct a human evaluation with teachers to assess the quality and usefulness of outputs from combining CTG and question taxonomies.

applications.justification: The significant application of the paper is the generation of educational questions using large language models, evaluated for their effectiveness in real classroom settings.
applications.quote: We investigate if LLMs can generate different types of questions from a given context that teachers think are appropriate for use in the classroom.
